task.title: Run OpenD with Docker Compose
task.shortdesc: The smallest install: the app, the build worker and Postgres on one host, from the Compose file in the repository.

prereq.p: You need Docker with Compose, a checkout of , and a host name readers can reach over HTTPS (terminate TLS in a reverse proxy in front of port 3000).

step.cmd: Create the configuration from the examples.

stepxmp.codeblock: cp deploy/.env.example deploy/.env cp deploy/seed/seed.example.yaml deploy/seed/seed.yaml

info.p: Set at least PUBLIC_URL and a random SESSION_SECRET. For publishing set GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET; for reader sign-in, the OIDC_* variables; for the admin API, OPEND_ADMIN_TOKEN. Change POSTGRES_PASSWORD. See the environment variable reference.

step.cmd: Edit deploy/seed/seed.yaml with your docs repository, organizations, entitlements and readers.

stepresult.p: Compose starts Postgres, runs the migrate service once to create the schema, then starts app on port 3000 (or OPEND_PORT) and worker. Both share the blobs volume at /data/blobs.

stepxmp.codeblock: docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml run --rm migrate seed /seed/seed.yaml

info.p: Seeding is idempotent: everything is upserted, so run it again after each change.

step.cmd: Connect GitHub and your identity provider.

result.p: Readers sign in at PUBLIC_URL and get the live release for their version's line. The first push to a release ref publishes it.
To evaluate without an identity provider, set NODE_ENV=development and OPEND_DEV_LOGIN=1, then sign in at /auth/dev as any seeded reader. Never do this with real content.
The web editor is an optional Compose profile, editor. See .
